Kit

Network profiles

5 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Choose by authority modelDefault timing and traffic budgetsMeasured framework limitsOverride profile valuesDirect component setup

A named network profile returns a kboot.Network_Config containing session and simulation-lane settings. Choose a profile for the authority model, inspect or override its fields, then pass the complete value to the generated attach procedure. Attachment validates the session and lane configuration together.

Odin
cfg := kboot.network_profile(.Listen_Server_Action)
cfg.session.max_players = 4
cfg.lane.smooth_cut = 48
cfg.lane.rewind_max = 30

my_game_net_attach(self, kboot.Options{
	title = "MY GAME",
	env = "MY_GAME",
}, cfg)

rewind_max caps historical rewind for hit judgment. For each shooter, the authority computes a tighter window from measured RTT and jitter, input margin, snapshot cadence, and configured watch delay, with one cadence of interpolation-phase slack. Until clock sampling is established, competitive rewind judges the current state.

Omitting the third argument selects .Friends_Coop. Name the profile in game code so the authority and timing choice is visible at the attachment call.

Choose by authority model#

Profile Use it for What it assumes
.Friends_Coop Invited co-op, reliable shared state, owner-streamed movement Players are allowed to author their own fast state. The host still validates shared commands.
.Listen_Server_Action Player-hosted action games using server simulation and prediction Clients send inputs; the listen host decides outcomes. The hosting player still controls the authority process.
.Dedicated_Competitive An action game refereed by an avatarless server Clients are adversarial and the authority runs on infrastructure they do not control. Every simulation input class must use @(gd_input) constraints or a semantic validator.

Run .Dedicated_Competitive with kboot.boot_serve on trusted infrastructure. Using that profile with boot_host still gives authority to the hosting player. The application supplies encryption, account identity, moderation, deployment policy, and game-specific command predicates.

The generated attach knows whether the game has a simulation lane and whether all of its input classes have generated @(gd_input) constraints or an authored validator. It refuses a dedicated profile with an unvalidated input class before the network starts:

Odin
@(gd_input)
Player_Input :: struct {
	move: [2]i8 `gd:"range=-1:1"`,
}

@(gd_sample)
player_sample :: proc(self: ^Game, tick: u64, input: ^Player_Input) {
	// Read local controls.
}

Decoding reconstructs Player_Input; the generated sanitizer applies its declared value constraints. Add a sample validator when validity depends on several fields or game state.

Default timing and traffic budgets#

All three profiles use bounded admission and the generated wire fingerprint gate. Their main timing choices are:

| Profile | Session rate | Session interpolation | Sim / snapshot rate | History | Rewind limit | Future-input limit | Watched delay | Snapshot budget | | --- | ---: | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Friends co-op | 20 Hz | fixed 150 ms | 60 / 20 Hz | 128 ticks | 250 ms | 64 ticks | 100 ms | 64 KiB/recipient | | Listen-server action | 20 Hz | adaptive 150–400 ms | 60 / 20 Hz | 128 ticks | 400 ms | 64 ticks | 100 ms | 32 KiB/recipient | | Dedicated competitive | 20 Hz | adaptive 100–250 ms | 60 / 30 Hz | 128 ticks | 250 ms | 24 ticks | 67 ms | 24 KiB/recipient |

Authority-ingress budgets are token buckets; rates below are per seated peer (actions is per stable player seat). The friends profile allows a two-second reliable burst for loading/transfer spikes; the others are tighter:

Profile Reliable ingress Stream ingress Action ingress
Friends co-op 512 pkt/s, 2 MiB/s 240 pkt/s, 2 MiB/s 64 act/s, 256 KiB/s
Listen-server action 256 pkt/s, 1 MiB/s 240 pkt/s, 2 MiB/s 60 act/s, 256 KiB/s
Dedicated competitive 128 pkt/s, 512 KiB/s 120 pkt/s, 1 MiB/s 30 act/s, 128 KiB/s

The dedicated profile also shortens command and join timeouts, requires a bounded player count, and refuses Session_Config.fingerprint = ksess.FINGERPRINT_NONE. Its tighter future-input limit reduces how far an untrusted client can stamp work ahead of authority time.

The profiles deliberately leave co-op outbound stream_budget = 0: an owner-stream budget requires a game-authored interest function. Simulation snapshot budgets are safe without AOI and are enabled above; they prioritize owned/stale rows and force a full row after deferral or AOI re-entry. Public games should still install AOI. traffic.stream is the distinct bounded client-to-authority ingress shown above.

Measured framework limits#

network_profile_envelope(profile) reports the framework limits exercised by the engine-free benchmark gate. Measure the complete game before treating these limits as a deployment capacity: game logic, physics, engine nodes, transport overhead, and hardware contribute additional cost.

Profile Players Persistent replicated entities Hot entities per recipient/tick Predicted entities/client Forced replay
Friends co-op 8 2,000 500 0 0
Listen-server action 8 2,000 500 128 8 ticks
Dedicated competitive 8 2,000 500 512 8 ticks

tests/kitstress measures server CPU, application egress bytes, session resident/peak allocation, join/snapshot/resume cost, per-recipient AOI fanout, and reconciliation cost at increasing sizes. Its optimized native reference run exercises 2/100, 4/500, and 8/2,000 player/entity fanout cases plus 32/128/512 predicted entities. Its thresholds detect large cost regressions. Repeat the measurement on deployment hardware and include the engine/game frame before increasing the supported limits. “Hot” means dirty and inside one recipient's AOI in the same tick; unchanged and out-of-interest entities are sparse and do not consume snapshot rows.

Override profile values#

network_profile fills every timing field, including booleans. Assign an override on that returned value rather than relying on a lower-level “zero means default” convention:

Odin
cfg := kboot.network_profile(.Listen_Server_Action)
cfg.session.interp_adapt = false
cfg.session.interp_delay = 0.12
cfg.lane.echo_inputs = true
cfg.lane.tolerance = 0.5
my_game_net_attach(self, opts, cfg)

The complete value is validated before boot_attach or lane_init. Validation covers positive rates and durations, adaptive interpolation floor/ceiling, bounded history indices, redundancy wire limits, the 31-tick watched-offset ceiling, smoothing values, and trust-profile requirements. Predict-world input echo also requires positive float tolerance; exact held-input comparison would otherwise trigger reconciliation on nearly every snapshot.

Build overrides by editing a value returned from network_profile. A partial Network_Config{...} literal is rejected rather than silently combining two different default systems.

Direct component setup#

The generated <game>_net_attach wrapper is the usual entry point. A game managing component lifetimes directly can configure the same settings before attachment:

Odin
cfg := kboot.network_configure(
	&self.ses,
	kboot.network_profile(.Listen_Server_Action),
	kboot.Network_Capabilities{
		has_lane = true,
		all_inputs_validated = true,
	},
)
kboot.boot_attach(&self.boot, self.owner, &self.ses, &self.comms, opts)
my_game_lane_init(self, &self.lane, &self.ses, cfg = cfg.lane)
kboot.boot_lane(&self.boot, &self.lane)

godot:kit/netcfg contains the engine-free implementation and can be imported directly for tooling or tests. kit/boot re-exports its game-facing types and procedures so game scripts can use the kboot import for that setup.
